extracted.intended_audience: readers/students/scholars of medieval Italian municipal history (Bologna)
extracted.subtask_description: Excerpt from a historical account describing Bologna's medieval institutions, laws, magistracies, and specific legal acts (e.g., 1257 manumission decree). Useful for understanding municipal constitution, legislative procedure, and social-legal reforms in medieval Bologna.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreigners' citizenship requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The foreigners, who were of these companies, were made citizens of Bologna, if they had been householders ten years in the city, and might be of the council of the commons, stewards of companies, and magistrates, equally with other citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condition for naturalization/municipal citizenship: ten years' householding in the city; upon meeting it, foreigners enjoyed equal civic rights (eligibility for council of the commons, stewardship of companies, magistracies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of constitutional instruments (reformations, privileges, decrees, statutes)
rubrics_metrics.description: All these particulars of their constitution were found in the ancient customs, or the privileges granted or confirmed by the emperors, or in the decrees of the councils, or in the laws of the city: the former were called reformations, the latter statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes sources of municipal law: (1) ancient customs (reformations), (2) imperial privileges, (3) council decrees, (4) city laws/statutes. This classification frames what counts as legitimate constitutional/administrative authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decrees versus laws and legislative procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The decrees were those ordinances which, at the prayer of the pretor, were accepted by the councils, or made by him, and approved by them. The laws were no other than the ordinances made by the legislators, which were called statutieri, or lawgivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational distinction and process: decrees arise from the pretor and council approval; laws arise from designated legislators ('statutieri'). Legislators were deputed from time to time, reviewed and reformed old laws (after the example of the Athenians), and the laws made were reported to the council, publicly recited, and written into volumes ('Statute Books').

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording and preservation of laws (Statute Books)
rubrics_metrics.description: The laws which these legislators made were reported to the council, by them recited publicly to the people, and written in the volumes of Civil Reason, which were called the Statute Books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement that laws be publicly recited and committed to written statute compilations (Statute Books) for preservation and public knowledge; this is presented as the mechanism for codification and continuity (constitution preserved until after 1250).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concentration of powers in the single council (constitutional design)
rubrics_metrics.description: All authority, legislative, executive, and judicial, was in one council, for when the special and general council met together they acted as one, and when one met alone it acted as sovereign: the podesta, and his judges and notaries, were only deputies of the council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes institutional concentration (one council as sovereign) and the subordinate/deputy status of magistrates; the narrative treats this concentration as an essential constitutional feature and criticizes it as a root fault that contributed to civic miseries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-ambition precautions in magistracy selection
rubrics_metrics.description: By mixing lot with choice, by rotations, and other prudent precautions, to prevent ambition, faction, and sedition from entering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design principles for selecting office-holders: combine sortition and election, rotate offices, and employ other checks to reduce ambition/faction; the text notes these precautions were often ineffectual in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of civil and military functions (prefect vs pretor)
rubrics_metrics.description: It was ordained, that the pretor should have the authority and jurisdiction of the city, and be superintendent of the councils of the commons, and that the captain should administer in war abroad; that within the city the councils of the people should govern, and confer in the public business with the antiani.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional allocation of roles: pretor = civil/judicial authority and council supervision; captain/prefect = military commander abroad; councils/antiani = municipal governance within the city. This separation is prescribed to distribute functions between civil and martial spheres.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manumission decree (1257 'Paradise of Pleasure'): emancipation and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: By decree of 3 June, 1257, all the slaves and villains were manumitted, and taxed annually in a certain quantity of corn, which was consigned to the care of an officer called the pretor of the sack; after a diligent examination, no one constrained in any kind of slavery in the city or episcopacy shall dare to remain or be detained in it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major social-legal reform: universal municipal manumission subject to registration, taxation in kind (corn) administered by a designated officer, and a prohibition on holding persons in servitude within the city/diocese after due examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manumission pricing and notarial memorial requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The memorial contains the names of all the masters and all the slaves, both male and female, ... ten pounds for those of more than fourteen years of age, whether men or women, and eight pounds for all under that age, to every master, for every one whom he holds in servitude. This memorial was written by me, Conrad Sclariti, a notary, deputed to the office of servants and maids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary schedule required for redemption (10 pounds for >14; 8 pounds for <14 per slave) and formal documentation: an official memorial/notarial record listing masters and slaves, created by a deputed notary and preserved as a public monument of the transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imola judicial arrangement with Bologna (delegation and fee-for-justice)
rubrics_metrics.description: They ordered that for the future they should have no pretor at all, and that all their differences should be brought before the pretor of Bologna, to be adjudged with equity and celerity, upon condition that they should pay the auditors or judges who should hear their controversies five hundred pounds a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example of inter-municipal judicial delegation: Imola surrendered local praetorship to central pretor of Bologna in exchange for adjudication by Bologna judges, subject to an annual payment (500 pounds) for the auditors — a procedural/financial arrangement to secure equitable and speedy justice and reduce local violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of impartial three-man magistracy to resolve noble disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: A new magistracy was created in the city of three men, who were to hear and prudently examine the differences among the nobles; Andalo, Malavolti, and Ramponi were chosen. These, without respect of persons, judging with impartiality, had a wonderful effect in the city, and with great mildness composed many discords and long enmities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional response to factional violence: appoint a small, balanced, and reputedly impartial panel (three magistrates from different factional affinities) charged to investigate and reconcile noble disputes; emphasized personal qualities (candour, prudence, impartiality) and demonstrable effectiveness.
